extracted.intended_audience: corporate registrants (issuers) and their counsel/accountants preparing SEC registration statements and periodic reports
extracted.subtask_description: Preparation of required disclosure under Regulation S-K (Items 202, 302, 303, 304) for securities descriptions, supplementary financial information, MD&A, and changes/disagreements with accountants in SEC filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trustee information and material relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of the trustee(s) and the nature of any material relationship with the registrant or with any of its affiliates; the percentage of securities of the class necessary to require the trustee to take action; and what indemnification the trustee may require before proceeding to enforce the lien.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide trustee identity, any material relationships to registrant/affiliates, voting/threshold percentage to compel trustee action, and indemnification terms trustee may demand prior to enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warrants and rights — required disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: If the securities described are to be offered pursuant to warrants or rights state: (1) the amount of securities called for by such warrants or rights; (2) the period during which and the price at which the warrants or rights are exercisable; (3) the amount of warrants or rights outstanding; (4) provisions for changes to or adjustments in the exercise price; and (5) any other material terms of such rights on warrants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose quantity, exercise period and price, outstanding amounts, adjustment provisions (anti-dilution, etc.), and any other material economic or procedural terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other securities — brief comparable description
rubrics_metrics.description: If securities other than capital stock, debt, warrants or rights are to be registered, include a brief description (comparable to that required in paragraphs (a), (b) and (c) of Item 202) of the rights evidenced thereby.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide information comparable in character and detail to that required for shares, debt, or warrants — sufficient to understand rights and risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market information for securities other than common equity
rubrics_metrics.description: If securities other than common equity are to be registered and there is an established public trading market for such securities provide market information with respect to such securities comparable to that required by paragraph (a) of Item 201 of Regulation S-K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an established market exists, furnish trading/market data (e.g., high/low, volume, market on which listed) analogous to Item 201(a) for common equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) — required disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: If Depositary Shares represented by American Depositary Receipts are being registered, furnish: (1) the name of the depositary and the address of its principal executive office; (2) state the title of the ADRs and identify the deposited security; describe briefly the terms of deposit, including provisions with respect to (i) amount of deposited securities per ADR, (ii) voting procedure, (iii) collection and distribution of dividends, (iv) transmission of notices/reports/proxy materials, (v) sale or exercise of rights, (vi) deposit or sale of securities from dividends/splits/reorgs, (vii) amendment/extension/termination of the deposit, (viii) rights to inspect transfer books and list of holders, (ix) restrictions on deposit/withdrawal, (x) limitation upon liability of the depositary; (3) describe all fees and charges which may be imposed directly or indirectly against the holder of the ADRs, indicating type of service, amount, and to whom paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address each enumerated subpoint (i)-(x) and fully disclose any fees and charges; Instruction 5 to Item 202 further specifies fee categories and that fees that can be collected against dividends and deposited securities should be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title/character of securities — shares information (Instruction 1.A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wherever the title of securities is required to be stated, provide, in the case of shares: the par or stated value, if any; the rate of dividends, if fixed, and whether cumulative or non-cumulative; a brief indication of the preference, if any; and if convertible or redeemable, a statement to that effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For share offerings, clearly state basic economic terms (par value, dividend rate/type, preference, convertibility/redeemability) so readers understand the security's character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title/character of securities — debt information (Instruction 1.B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where title is required, in the case of debt, provide the rate of interest; the date of maturity or indication of serial maturities; if payment of principal or interest is contingent, an indication of such contingency; a brief indication of the priority of the issue; and, if convertible or callable, a statement to that effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For debt instruments disclose coupon, maturities (or serial maturity structure), contingencies, priority relative to other indebtedness, and convertibility/callability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title/character of securities — other kinds (Instruction 1.C)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of any other kind of security, appropriate information of comparable character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For non-standard securities supply information comparable in substance to that required for shares or debt to convey the security's economic and legal features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign registrant additional disclosures (Instruction 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant is a foreign registrant, include: (A) a brief description of any limitations on the right of nonresident or foreign owners to hold or vote such securities; (B) a brief description of any governmental laws, decrees or regulations in the country affecting remittance of dividends, interest and other payments to nonresident holders; (C) a brief outline of all taxes, including withholding provisions, to which U.S. security holders are subject under existing laws/regulations of the foreign country; and (D) a brief description of pertinent provisions of any reciprocal tax treaty between such foreign country and the United States regarding withholding or, if there is no such treaty, so state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For foreign registrants, disclose ownership/voting limits, cross-border payment restrictions, tax consequences for U.S. holders, and treaty treatment (or absence thereof).

rubrics_metrics.name: Convertible securities/warrants subject to redemption or call (Instruction 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where convertible securities or stock purchase warrants are being registered that are subject to redemption or call, disclose: (A) whether the right to convert or purchase will be forfeited unless exercised before the date specified in a notice of redemption or call; (B) the expiration or termination date of the warrants; (C) the kinds, frequency and timing of notice of the redemption or call, including cities or newspapers of publication (or a description of discretion provided to registrant); and (D) in the case of bearer securities, that investors are responsible for arrangements to prevent loss of conversion/purchase rights in the event of redemption/call (for example, by reading the newspapers where notice may be published).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When redemption/call features exist, fully disclose conversion forfeiture conditions, expiration dates, notice mechanics (publication venues), and bearer-security investor responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADRs — specific fee disclosures required (Instruction 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: The response to paragraph (f) shall include information with respect to fees and charges in connection with (A) the deposit or substitution of the underlying securities; (B) receipt and distribution of dividends; (C) the sale or exercise of rights; (D) the withdrawal of the underlying security; and (E) the transferring, splitting or grouping of receipts. Information with respect to the right to collect the fees and charges against dividends received and deposited securities shall be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List fee types, amounts, and payees for each category (A-E) and state whether fees may be collected against dividends or deposited securities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange listing identification — caution against implying listing will be obtained
rubrics_metrics.description: If the securities being described have been accepted for listing on an exchange, the exchange may be identified. The document should not, however, convey the impression that the registrant may apply successfully for listing of the securities on an exchange or that, in the case of an underwritten offering, the underwriters may request the registrant to apply for such listing, unless there is reasonable assurance that the securities to be offered will be acceptable to a securities exchange for listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may name an exchange if accepted, but avoid statements that imply likelihood of future listing unless reasonable assurance exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of material quarterly changes (Item 302(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: When there are one or more retrospective changes to the statements of comprehensive income for any of the quarters within the two most recent fiscal years or any subsequent interim period that individually or in the aggregate are material, provide an explanation of the reasons for such material changes and disclose, for each affected quarterly period and the fourth quarter in the affected year, summarized financial information related to the statements of comprehensive income and earnings per share reflecting such changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow PCAOB auditing standards if an accountant reported on the statements; the requirement applies to registrants with securities registered under Sections 12(b) or 12(g) (except mutual life insurers); smaller reporting companies are exempt. Provide explanation and adjusted summaries including EPS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information about oil and gas producing activities (Item 302(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants engaged in oil and gas producing activities shall present the information about oil and gas producing activities specified in FASB ASC Topic 932, if such activities are regarded as significant under tests set forth in FASB ASC Subtopic 932-235 for 'Significant Activities.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the ASC 932 disclosures for annual and balance-sheet dates per Instruction 1; see Regulation S-X cross-references and note exemptions for DOE-exempt entities per Instruction 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smaller reporting company exemptions (Item 302/303)
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant that qualifies as a smaller reporting company is not required to provide the information required by Item 302 and certain Item 303 disclosures (as specified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If qualifying as a smaller reporting company under §229.10(f)(1), note the reduced disclosure obligations and follow the specified limited-period requirements in related instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: MD&A objective (Item 303(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of the discussion and analysis is to provide material information relevant to an assessment of the financial condition and results of operations of the registrant including an evaluation of the amounts and certainty of cash flows from operations and from outside sources. The discussion must focus specifically on material events and uncertainties known to management that are reasonably likely to cause reported financial information not to be necessarily indicative of future operating results or of future financial condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MD&A should explain matters that had a material impact and those reasonably likely to have material impact on future operations, enhancing a reader's understanding from management's perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: MD&A — full fiscal years: coverage and segment/subdivision focus (Item 303(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The discussion of financial condition, changes in financial condition and results of operations must provide information as specified in paragraphs (b)(1) through (3) and such other information that the registrant believes to be necessary to an understanding. Where financial statements reflect material changes from period-to-period, describe underlying reasons in quantitative and qualitative terms. If discussion of segment information and/or other subdivisions is necessary, focus on each relevant reportable segment and/or subdivision and on the registrant as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide both quantitative and qualitative explanations for material period-to-period changes; include segment/disclosure when necessary for understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liquidity and capital resources (Item 303(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze the registrant's ability to generate and obtain adequate amounts of cash to meet its requirements and its plans for cash in the short-term (next 12 months) and separately in the long-term (beyond 12 months). The discussion should analyze material cash requirements from known contractual and other obligations, specifying the type of obligation and the relevant time period. Provide liquidity (identify trends, demands, commitments, events or uncertainties likely to increase/decrease liquidity and actions to remedy deficiencies; identify internal and external sources and unused sources) and capital resources (describe material cash requirements including capital expenditures, anticipated sources of funds, general purpose; describe known material trends in capital resources and changes in mix and relative cost).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish short-term vs long-term needs, specify obligations by type/timeframe, disclose cures for deficiencies, and discuss mix of financing (equity/debt/off-balance-sheet) and likely changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results of operations (Item 303(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any unusual or infrequent events or transactions or any significant economic changes that materially affected reported income from continuing operations and indicate extent of effect; describe other significant components of revenues or expenses material to understanding results. Describe any known trends or uncertainties that have had or are reasonably likely to have a material favorable or unfavorable impact on net sales/revenues or income; if known events are reasonably likely to cause material change in relationship between costs and revenues, disclose them. If material changes in net sales or revenue, describe extent attributable to changes in prices vs changes in volume/new products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain causes of material changes, separate one-time items from ongoing operations, and attribute revenue changes to price/volume/new products when material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical accounting estimates (Item 303(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical accounting estimates are those estimates made in accordance with GAAP that involve significant estimation uncertainty and have had or are reasonably likely to have a material impact. Provide qualitative and quantitative information necessary to understand estimation uncertainty and the impact the estimate has had or is reasonably likely to have on financial condition/results, including why each estimate is subject to uncertainty and, to the extent material and reasonably available, how much each estimate/assumption has changed over a relevant period and the sensitivity of the reported amount to the methods, assumptions and estimates underlying its calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each critical estimate disclose why it is uncertain, magnitude of historical change where available, and sensitivity analysis showing how results change with key assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: MD&A presentation and non-duplication requirements (Instructions to paragraph (b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion must cover the periods presented; registrant may use any presentation that enhances understanding. No repetition of reasons is required across related line items; registrants need not recite amounts readily computable from the financial statements; discussion must not merely repeat numerical data; provide analysis in a format that facilitates understanding and supplements, not duplicates, disclosure already provided; for critical accounting estimates, supplement but do not duplicate accounting policy notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for analysis and context rather than restating numbers; use clear format; avoid redundant disclosure that merely repeats footnotes or financial statement amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: MD&A — off-balance sheet arrangements and commitments (Instruction 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of commitments or obligations, including contingent obligations, arising from arrangements with unconsolidated entities or persons that have or are reasonably likely to have a material current or future effect on the registrant's financial condition, changes in financial condition, revenues or expenses, results of operations, liquidity, cash requirements or capital resources must be provided even when the arrangement results in no obligations being reported in the registrant's consolidated balance sheets. Examples include guarantees; retained or contingent interests in assets transferred; contractual arrangements that support credit, liquidity or market risk for transferred assets; obligations from variable interests in an unconsolidated entity; or obligations related to derivative instruments indexed to and classified in registrant's own equity under U.S. GAAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe off-balance-sheet exposures and commitments with material potential effects even if not reflected as liabilities in consolidated statements; give examples and explain potential impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: MD&A — foreign private issuer considerations (Instructions 9 and 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant is a foreign private issuer, briefly discuss any pertinent governmental economic, fiscal, monetary, or political policies or factors that have materially affected or could materially affect operations or investments by U.S. nationals, consider impact of hyperinflation if occurred, and focus discussion on primary financial statements presented including reconciliation to U.S. GAAP and aspects of differences necessary for understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign issuers must highlight host-country policy risks, hyperinflation effects, and explain material differences between local GAAP and U.S. GAAP when relevant to understanding the primary financial statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes in and disagreements with accountants — disclosure upon resignation/dismissal (Item 304(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: If during the two most recent fiscal years or any subsequent interim period an independent accountant previously engaged as principal accountant has resigned, declined to stand for re‑election, or was dismissed, the registrant shall: (i) state whether the former accountant resigned/declined/was dismissed and the date; (ii) state whether the principal accountant's report for either of the past two years contained an adverse opinion or disclaimer or was qualified/modified as to uncertainty/audit scope/accounting principles and describe the nature of each; (iii) state whether the decision to change accountants was recommended/approved by any audit or similar committee or board; (iv) state whether there were any disagreements with the former accountant on any matter of accounting principles/practices/financial statement disclosure/auditing scope or procedure, describe each such disagreement, state whether audit committee/board discussed them, and state whether the registrant authorized the former accountant to respond fully to successor inquiries or describe any limitation; (v) provide information for each of the reportable events listed (A)-(D) that occurred within the two most recent fiscal years and any subsequent interim period preceding the former accountant's resignation/declination/dismissal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the nature and dates of change, audit opinions/modifications, committee/board approval, detailed description of disagreements (resolved or not), and any reportable events (see A-D) even if unrelated to disagreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reportable events related to accountant change (Item 304(a)(1)(v) A–D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reportable events include: (A) the accountant's having advised registrant that the internal controls necessary for reliable financial statements do not exist; (B) the accountant's having advised that information has come to its attention making it unwilling to be associated with management's financial statements; (C) the accountant's having advised of the need to expand significantly the scope of its audit or that information has come to attention that if investigated may (i) materially impact fairness/reliability of a previously issued audit report or underlying financials or (ii) cause it to be unwilling to rely on management's representations, and due to resignation/dismissal the accountant did not expand scope or investigate further; (D) the accountant's having advised information materially impacts fairness/reliability of a previously issued audit report or underlying financials or later financial statements and, due to resignation/dismissal, the issue has not been resolved to the accountant's satisfaction prior to its departure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose these specific categories of serious audit-related events and any related disagreements or unresolved issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes in and disagreements with accountants — disclosure upon engagement of new accountant (Item 304(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a new independent accountant has been engaged as principal accountant, the registrant shall identify the newly engaged accountant and the date of engagement. In addition, if during the two most recent fiscal years the registrant consulted the newly engaged accountant regarding (i) the application of accounting principles to a specified transaction or the type of audit opinion that might be rendered, or (ii) any matter that was the subject of a disagreement or a reportable event, then the registrant shall: state and identify the issues; briefly describe the views of the newly engaged accountant as expressed orally or in writing and, if written views were received, file them as an exhibit; state whether the former accountant was consulted and, if so, provide a summary of the former accountant's views; and request the newly engaged accountant to review the disclosure and provide a letter to the Commission which the registrant shall file as an exhibit if furnished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify new accountant/date, disclose prior consultations on accounting/audit-opinion issues or disagreements, include or file written views as exhibits, summarize former accountant views, and obtain/attach the new accountant's letter if provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Former accountant letter and filing timing (Item 304(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The registrant shall provide the former accountant with a copy of the disclosures it is making in response to Item 304(a) no later than the day the disclosures are filed, request the former accountant to furnish a letter to the Commission stating whether it agrees with the statements made and, if not, stating the respects in which it does not agree, and file the former accountant's letter as an exhibit. If the former accountant's letter is unavailable at filing, request it promptly so registrant can file the letter within ten business days after filing; notwithstanding the ten-business-day period, the registrant shall file the letter by amendment within two business days of receipt; the former accountant may provide an interim letter highlighting areas of concern and indicate a more detailed letter will follow within the ten business day period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide disclosures to former accountant at filing, request and attach its response letter as an exhibit, and follow the specified timing rules for filing the accountant's letter or interim letter.
